subject.title: fix(gateway): clients can identify authorization failures

question: Should gateway authorization denials preserve the existing `INVALID_REQUEST` top-level code with additive details, or should the protocol formally adopt `FORBIDDEN` as a versioned/negotiated behavior change?
rationale: The PR’s central semantic-code change affects existing protocol consumers, and repository policy requires additive handling or explicit follow-through for incompatible gateway protocol changes.

options.title: Add details without changing the top-level code
options.body: Keep `INVALID_REQUEST` for existing clients and use the new discriminated details object for clients that need reliable authorization classification.

options.title: Adopt `FORBIDDEN` with protocol follow-through
options.body: Version or negotiate the changed response semantics and update supported clients, compatibility tests, and upgrade documentation accordingly.

recommendation.title: Add details without changing the top-level code
recommendation.body: Keep `INVALID_REQUEST` for existing clients and use the new discriminated details object for clients that need reliable authorization classification.

likelyOwner.reason: Authored the current gateway authorization contract proposal and is the only evidence-backed routing candidate available from the supplied history.
